passages.text: Now Abram’s wife Sarai had borne him no children, but she had an Egyptian maidservant named Hagar.
passages.sermon:
Abram had a wife named Sarai.
Sarai could not have children.
Sarai had a maidservant.
The maidservant was Egyptian.
Her name was Hagar.
passages.original: וְשָׂרַי֙ אֵ֣שֶׁת אַבְרָ֔ם לֹ֥א יָלְדָ֖ה ל֑וֹ וְלָ֛הּ שִׁפְחָ֥ה מִצְרִ֖ית וּשְׁמָ֥הּ הָגָֽר׃

passages.text: So Sarai said to Abram, “Look now, the LORD has prevented me from bearing children. Please go to my maidservant; perhaps I can build a family by her.” And Abram listened to the voice of Sarai.
passages.sermon:
Sarai was Abram’s wife.
Sarai could not have children.
Sarai spoke to Abram.
Sarai said, “The LORD has kept me from having children.”
Sarai said, “Go to my maidservant.”
Sarai said, “Maybe I can have a family through her.”
Abram listened to Sarai.
passages.original: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר שָׂרַ֜י אֶל־ אַבְרָ֗ם הִנֵּה־ נָ֞א עֲצָרַ֤נִי יְהוָה֙ מִלֶּ֔דֶת בֹּא־ נָא֙ אֶל־ שִׁפְחָתִ֔י אוּלַ֥י אִבָּנֶ֖ה מִמֶּ֑נָּה וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע אַבְרָ֖ם לְק֥וֹל שָׂרָֽי׃

passages.text: So after he had lived in Canaan for ten years, his wife Sarai took her Egyptian maidservant Hagar and gave her to Abram to be his wife.
passages.sermon:
Abram was Sarai’s husband.
Sarai was Abram’s wife.
Sarai had a maidservant named Hagar.
Hagar was Egyptian.
Abram and Sarai had lived in Canaan for ten years.
After ten years in Canaan, Sarai took Hagar.
Sarai gave Hagar to Abram.
Sarai gave Hagar to Abram to be his wife.
passages.original: וַתִּקַּ֞ח שָׂרַ֣י אֵֽשֶׁת־ אַבְרָ֗ם אֶת־ הָגָ֤ר הַמִּצְרִית֙ שִׁפְחָתָ֔הּ מִקֵּץ֙ עֶ֣שֶׂר שָׁנִ֔ים לְשֶׁ֥בֶת אַבְרָ֖ם בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן וַתִּתֵּ֥ן אֹתָ֛הּ לְאַבְרָ֥ם אִישָׁ֖הּ ל֥וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃

passages.text: And he slept with Hagar, and she conceived. But when Hagar realized that she was pregnant, she began to despise her mistress.
passages.sermon:
Abram slept with Hagar.
Hagar conceived a child.
Hagar realized she was pregnant.
Hagar began to despise Sarai, her mistress.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֥א אֶל־ הָגָ֖ר וַתַּ֑הַר וַתֵּ֙רֶא֙ כִּ֣י הָרָ֔תָה וַתֵּקַ֥ל גְּבִרְתָּ֖הּ בְּעֵינֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: Then Sarai said to Abram, “May the wrong done to me be upon you! I delivered my servant into your arms, and ever since she saw that she was pregnant, she has treated me with contempt. May the LORD judge between you and me.”
passages.sermon:
Sarai was Abram’s wife.
Sarai spoke to Abram.
Sarai said, “I am suffering because of you.”
Sarai said, “I gave my servant to you.”
Sarai said, “My servant saw that she became pregnant.”
Sarai said, “Now I am unimportant in her eyes.”
Sarai said, “May the LORD judge between you and me.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר שָׂרַ֣י אֶל־ אַבְרָם֮ חֲמָסִ֣י עָלֶיךָ֒ אָנֹכִ֗י נָתַ֤תִּי שִׁפְחָתִי֙ בְּחֵיקֶ֔ךָ וַתֵּ֙רֶא֙ כִּ֣י הָרָ֔תָה וָאֵקַ֖ל בְּעֵינֶ֑יהָ יִשְׁפֹּ֥ט יְהוָ֖ה בֵּינִ֥י וּבֵינֶֽיׄךָ׃

passages.text: “Here,” said Abram, “your servant is in your hands. Do whatever you want with her.” Then Sarai treated Hagar so harshly that she fled from her.
passages.sermon:
Abram was Sarai’s husband.
Sarai had a servant named Hagar.
Abram spoke to Sarai.
Abram said, “Your servant is in your hands.”
Abram told Sarai, “Do whatever is good in your eyes to her.”
Sarai treated Hagar harshly.
Hagar fled from Sarai.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אַבְרָ֜ם אֶל־ שָׂרַ֗י הִנֵּ֤ה שִׁפְחָתֵךְ֙ בְּיָדֵ֔ךְ עֲשִׂי־ לָ֖הּ הַטּ֣וֹב בְּעֵינָ֑יִךְ וַתְּעַנֶּ֣הָ שָׂרַ֔י וַתִּבְרַ֖ח מִפָּנֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: Now the angel of the LORD found Hagar by a spring of water in the desert—the spring along the road to Shur.
passages.sermon:
The angel of the LORD found Hagar.
Hagar was by a spring of water.
The spring was in the desert.
The spring was along the road to Shur.
passages.original: וַֽיִּמְצָאָ֞הּ מַלְאַ֧ךְ יְהוָ֛ה עַל־ עֵ֥ין הַמַּ֖יִם בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר עַל־ הָעַ֖יִן בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ שֽׁוּר׃

passages.text: “Hagar, servant of Sarai,” he said, “where have you come from, and where are you going?” “I am running away from my mistress Sarai,” she replied.
passages.sermon:
The angel of the LORD spoke to Hagar.
Hagar was the servant of Sarai.
The angel said, “Hagar, servant of Sarai, where have you come from?”
The angel also said, “Where are you going?”
Hagar answered, “I am running away from my mistress Sarai.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמַ֗ר הָגָ֞ר שִׁפְחַ֥ת שָׂרַ֛י אֵֽי־ מִזֶּ֥ה בָ֖את וְאָ֣נָה תֵלֵ֑כִי וַתֹּ֕אמֶר מִפְּנֵי֙ שָׂרַ֣י גְּבִרְתִּ֔י אָנֹכִ֖י בֹּרַֽחַת׃

passages.text: So the angel of the LORD told her, “Return to your mistress and submit to her authority.”
passages.sermon:
The angel of the LORD spoke to Hagar.
Hagar was Sarai’s servant.
The angel said, “Return to your mistress.”
The angel said, “Submit to her authority.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהּ֙ מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה שׁ֖וּבִי אֶל־ גְּבִרְתֵּ֑ךְ וְהִתְעַנִּ֖י תַּ֥חַת יָדֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: Then the angel added, “I will greatly multiply your offspring so that they will be too numerous to count.”
passages.sermon:
The angel of the LORD spoke to Hagar.
Hagar was the servant of Sarai.
The angel said, “I will make your descendants very many.”
No one will be able to count them because they will be so numerous.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהּ֙ מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה הַרְבָּ֥ה אַרְבֶּ֖ה אֶת־ זַרְעֵ֑ךְ וְלֹ֥א יִסָּפֵ֖ר מֵרֹֽב׃

passages.text: The angel of the LORD proceeded: “Behold, you have conceived and will bear a son. And you shall name him Ishmael, for the LORD has heard your cry of affliction.
passages.sermon:
The angel of the LORD spoke to Hagar.
Hagar was an Egyptian servant of Sarai.
The angel said, “You are pregnant.
You will give birth to a son.
You must name him Ishmael.
The LORD has heard your suffering.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהּ֙ מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה הִנָּ֥ךְ הָרָ֖ה וְיֹלַ֣דְתְּ בֵּ֑ן וְקָרָ֤את שְׁמוֹ֙ יִשְׁמָעֵ֔אל כִּֽי־ שָׁמַ֥ע יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ עָנְיֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: He will be a wild donkey of a man, and his hand will be against everyone, and everyone’s hand against him; he will live in hostility toward all his brothers.”
passages.sermon:
The angel of the LORD spoke about Ishmael.
Ishmael will be a wild and untamed man.
He will fight against everyone.
Everyone will fight against him.
He will live in conflict with all his brothers.
passages.original: וְה֤וּא יִהְיֶה֙ פֶּ֣רֶא אָדָ֔ם יָד֣וֹ בַכֹּ֔ל וְיַ֥ד כֹּ֖ל בּ֑וֹ וְעַל־ פְּנֵ֥י כָל־ אֶחָ֖יו יִשְׁכֹּֽן׃

passages.text: So Hagar gave this name to the LORD who had spoken to her: “You are the God who sees me,” for she said, “Here I have seen the One who sees me!”
passages.sermon:
Hagar was an Egyptian servant of Sarai.
The LORD spoke to Hagar.
Hagar gave a name to the LORD who spoke to her.
She said, “You are the God who sees me.”
Hagar said this because she realized something.
She said, “Here I have seen the One who sees me.”
passages.original: וַתִּקְרָ֤א שֵׁם־ יְהוָה֙ הַדֹּבֵ֣ר אֵלֶ֔יהָ אַתָּ֖ה אֵ֣ל רֳאִ֑י כִּ֣י אָֽמְרָ֗ה הֲגַ֥ם הֲלֹ֛ם רָאִ֖יתִי אַחֲרֵ֥י רֹאִֽי׃

passages.text: Therefore the well was called Beer-lahai-roi. It is located between Kadesh and Bered.
passages.sermon: People gave the well a name.\r\nThey called the well Beer-lahai-roi.\r\nThis well stands between Kadesh and Bered.
passages.original: עַל־ כֵּן֙ קָרָ֣א לַבְּאֵ֔ר בְּאֵ֥ר לַחַ֖י רֹאִ֑י הִנֵּ֥ה בֵין־ קָדֵ֖שׁ וּבֵ֥ין בָּֽרֶד׃

passages.text: And Hagar bore Abram a son, and Abram gave the name Ishmael to the son she had borne.
passages.sermon:
Hagar was an Egyptian servant.
Abram was her master.
Hagar gave birth to a son for Abram.
Abram named the son Ishmael.
passages.original: וַתֵּ֧לֶד הָגָ֛ר לְאַבְרָ֖ם בֵּ֑ן וַיִּקְרָ֨א אַבְרָ֧ם שֶׁם־ בְּנ֛וֹ אֲשֶׁר־ יָלְדָ֥ה הָגָ֖ר יִשְׁמָעֵֽאל׃

passages.text: Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to him.
passages.sermon: Abram was eighty-six years old.\r\nHagar gave birth to a son for Abram.\r\nThey named the son Ishmael.
passages.original: וְאַבְרָ֕ם בֶּן־ שְׁמֹנִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וְשֵׁ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֑ים בְּלֶֽדֶת־ הָגָ֥ר אֶת־ יִשְׁמָעֵ֖אל לְאַבְרָֽם׃ס
